input.content:
# Architecture Overview — Fields Behavior Candidates and Before-use Cycle Checks

> architecture-overview · [m2ux/workflow-server#1692](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/pull/1692) · 2026-11-11

## Summary

The shared skill checker, `check_skill_files.py`, gains three checks: execution written inside a skill file's declared Fields section, Fields prose that reads as behavior, and cycles in the files a skill tells its reader to read first. All three land in the checker's per-file and skill-wide passes, and Work Planner's `rules.json` names them as the deciders of three house rules. A skill's contract sections can now be held to values-only, and its before-use reading order to an acyclic graph, by a machine check rather than review alone.

## Structure

The change reaches the checker's entry point `main`, its per-file pass `check`, and three new groups of functions the graph places in separate communities: Fields execution, Fields behavior candidates and before-use cycles. Each group reads a file's contract through the existing structure loader (`structure.json`, which declares a file's sections, including the `contracts` section, here `Fields`) and the existing Markdown scanner. Results reach the reader as findings, which fail the run, or review candidates, which print and fail nothing; the rule ledger `rules.json` maps house rules to finding kinds.

```mermaid
---
title: Components — Fields Behavior Candidates and Before-use Cycle Checks
---
flowchart LR
    Caller([CLI or test suite])
    Rules[(work-planner/rules.json)]

    subgraph Entry [Checker entry]
        Main[main]
        Check[check]
        Undecided[undecided_rules]
    end

    subgraph FieldsExec [Fields execution]
        Steps[fields_steps]
    end

    subgraph FieldsCand [Fields behavior candidates]
        Candidates[fields_candidates]
        Clauses[behavior_clauses]
        Sections[contract_sections]
    end

    subgraph BeforeUse [Before-use cycles]
        Findings[before_use_findings]
        Graph[before_use_graph]
        Reqs[requirements]
        Cycles[before_use_cycles]
    end

    subgraph Shared [Contract and scanning]
        Contract[contract / structure_at]
        Scan[scan / scan_blocks]
    end

    Caller -->|argv: skill roots| Main
    Main -->|each file| Check
    Check -->|file lines and entry| Steps
    Steps -->|section spans| Sections
    Main -->|each file| Candidates
    Candidates -->|field span| Clauses
    Candidates -->|section spans| Sections
    Main -->|all files| Findings
    Findings -->|paths| Graph
    Graph -->|file| Reqs
    Findings -->|graph| Cycles
    Candidates -->|path| Contract
    Graph -->|path| Contract
    Candidates -->|path| Scan
    Reqs -->|path| Scan
    Main -->|guide| Undecided
    Undecided -->|reads kinds| Rules

    style Main fill:#c8e6c9,stroke:#2e7d32
    style Check fill:#c8e6c9,stroke:#2e7d32
    style Steps fill:#c8e6c9,stroke:#2e7d32
    style Candidates fill:#c8e6c9,stroke:#2e7d32
    style Clauses fill:#c8e6c9,stroke:#2e7d32
    style Sections fill:#c8e6c9,stroke:#2e7d32
    style Findings fill:#c8e6c9,stroke:#2e7d32
    style Graph fill:#c8e6c9,stroke:#2e7d32
    style Reqs fill:#c8e6c9,stroke:#2e7d32
    style Cycles fill:#c8e6c9,stroke:#2e7d32
    style Rules fill:#c8e6c9,stroke:#2e7d32
    style Undecided fill:#f5f5f5,stroke:#9e9e9e
    style Contract fill:#f5f5f5,stroke:#9e9e9e
    style Scan fill:#f5f5f5,stroke:#9e9e9e
```

### Checker entry

- **main.**
  The command line: checks every Markdown file under the named skill roots. It now also collects before-use cycle findings and review candidates, prints candidates beside findings, and adds a candidate count to its summary line; only findings set exit status 1.
- **check.**
  The per-file pass. It now reports each `executable step in Fields` from `fields_steps`.
- **KINDS, CANDIDATES and OPERATIONS.**
  `KINDS` lists every finding kind; it gains `executable step in Fields` and `before-use cycle`. `CANDIDATES` is new and holds `Fields behavior candidate`. `OPERATIONS`, the names a `rules.json` entry may cite, is their union with `review`, so `undecided_rules` accepts the new names.

### Fields execution

- **fields_steps.**
  Inside a file's declared contract section, reports a numbered step, a numbered heading, or a call verb (`Run`, or the `Apply`/`Follow` verbs the file's `calls` declares) on a link to an operation or command. Fenced text and HTML invocations are skipped and keep their own kinds.

### Fields behavior candidates

- **contract_sections.**
  The span of each level-two heading whose title equals the file's `contracts` declaration.
- **behavior_clauses.**
  Splits a field's prose into sentences and tags each with behavior families (`acquire`, `write`, `route`, `transition`) from fixed word lists. It marks a sentence agentive (something performs the behavior) when an actor noun such as `caller` or `script` precedes a verb, or the sentence opens with an imperative. Tables, headings, fences and invocations are not read.
- **fields_candidates.**
  For each level-three field under the contract section, a candidate when at least one clause is agentive and the clauses together span two families. Each carries its clauses with line numbers and names the file's procedure section as possible owner.

### Before-use cycles

- **requirements and Requirement.**
  A `Requirement` is one explicit before-use edge: source file and line, target file and anchor, and the condition text. `requirements` collects three forms: a `Read [x](…) first.` or `Read [x](…) before …` sentence (`BEFORE_USE`), a link in a `## Prerequisites` section, and a declared `preamble` link in the file's introduction.
- **before_use_graph and read_span.**
  Builds nodes of (file, anchor) reachable from every checked file. A whole-file read takes every requirement in the file; a heading read takes only requirements in that section and the file introduction (`read_span`).
- **before_use_cycles.**
  Tarjan's strongly connected components over that graph, then one shortest closed witness per cyclic component.
- **before_use_findings.**
  One `before-use cycle` finding per witness, naming each node and the line of the requirement leaving it.

### Rule ledger

- **work-planner/rules.json.**
  `solid/callable-transformations` is decided by `executable step in Fields`, `solid/boundary-review` by `Fields behavior candidate`, and `solid/before-use-ordering` by `before-use cycle`, each still beside `review`.

## Behaviour

Three flows, one per check, all started by `main`.

### Fields execution

`check` runs it on each file; it yields findings that fail the run.

```mermaid
---
title: Sequence — Fields execution
---
sequenceDiagram
    participant Check as check
    participant Steps as fields_steps
    participant Op as operation_target
    participant Cmd as command_target
    participant Contract as contract / structure_at

    Check->>Steps: lines, headings, entry
    Steps->>Op: link target
    Op-->>Steps: operation or none
    Steps->>Cmd: link target
    Cmd->>Contract: target file's entry
    Contract-->>Cmd: entry
    Cmd-->>Steps: command or none
    Steps-->>Check: line, detail
```

- **Section selection.**
  Only lines between the `contracts` heading and the next heading of its level are read.
- **Call test.**
  A link counts as a call only when the verb directly precedes it and the target resolves to an operation or command, so a definition link is not execution.

### Fields behavior candidates

`main` runs it on each file after the per-file pass; it yields candidates that print only.

```mermaid
---
title: Sequence — Fields behavior candidates
---
sequenceDiagram
    participant Main as main
    participant Cand as fields_candidates
    participant Contract as contract / structure_at
    participant Sections as contract_sections
    participant Scan as scan / scan_blocks

    Main->>Cand: path, root, declared
    Cand->>Contract: path
    Contract-->>Cand: entry with contracts
    Cand->>Scan: path
    Scan-->>Cand: lines, fenced, headings
    Cand->>Sections: lines, headings, entry
    Sections-->>Cand: spans
    Cand-->>Main: candidates
```

- **Undeclared files.**
  A file whose entry declares no `contracts` returns no candidate.
- **Clause tagging.**
  `behavior_clauses` is a measured callee of `fields_candidates` but sits in no indexed flow, so it is described here rather than drawn: it runs once per level-three field inside each span.

### Before-use cycles

`main` runs it once over all files; each cycle is a finding that fails the run.

```mermaid
---
title: Sequence — Before-use cycles
---
sequenceDiagram
    participant Main as main
    participant Find as before_use_findings
    participant Graph as before_use_graph
    participant Span as read_span
    participant Cycles as before_use_cycles
    participant Named as named

    Main->>Find: files, declared
    Find->>Graph: paths
    Graph->>Span: path, anchor
    Span-->>Graph: line set
    Graph-->>Find: node to requirements
    Find->>Cycles: graph
    Cycles-->>Find: witnesses
    Find->>Named: node path
    Named-->>Find: display name
    Find-->>Main: findings
```

- **Graph growth.**
  `before_use_graph` follows each requirement's target, so files outside the checked roots that a requirement names (a shared `guidelines.md`, for example) enter the graph.
- **Witness.**
  Each strongly connected component with a cycle yields one witness, starting at its lexically first node and ordered by source line.

## What Changed

### Checker entry

- **main and check.**
  Report two new finding kinds and one non-failing candidate kind; the summary line counts candidates.

### Fields execution

- **fields_steps.**
  Holds a contract section to values: steps, numbered headings and operation calls there are findings.

### Fields behavior candidates

- **fields_candidates.**
  Points semantic review at fields whose prose performs two kinds of behavior.

### Before-use cycles

- **before_use_findings.**
  Rejects a cycle in the explicit read-first graph with a closed witness.

### Rule ledger

- **rules.json.**
  Three Work Planner house rules now name a machine check as a decider.

## Reading Order

1. **[skills/scripts/check_skill_files.py — module docstring](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/6fce88bdc343d55093d762daecc6557f1a7d5401/skills/scripts/check_skill_files.py#L73-L88)** — states the two new relations the code enforces.
2. **[skills/scripts/check_skill_files.py — main](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/6fce88bdc343d55093d762daecc6557f1a7d5401/skills/scripts/check_skill_files.py#L1759-L1818)** — where the new checks enter and how candidates differ from findings.
3. **[skills/scripts/check_skill_files.py — Fields checks](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/6fce88bdc343d55093d762daecc6557f1a7d5401/skills/scripts/check_skill_files.py#L1474-L1604)** — `contract_sections`, `fields_steps`, the behavior lexicon and `fields_candidates`.
4. **[skills/scripts/check_skill_files.py — before-use graph](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/6fce88bdc343d55093d762daecc6557f1a7d5401/skills/scripts/check_skill_files.py#L1607-L1756)** — requirement extraction, read spans, cycle search and findings.
5. **[skills/scripts/check_skill_files.py — KINDS and CANDIDATES](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/6fce88bdc343d55093d762daecc6557f1a7d5401/skills/scripts/check_skill_files.py#L177-L204)** — the kind registry `rules.json` is checked against.
6. **[skills/work-planner/rules.json](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/6fce88bdc343d55093d762daecc6557f1a7d5401/skills/work-planner/rules.json#L9-L16)** — the three rules that now cite the new kinds.
7. **[skills/test/test_check_skill_files.py](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/6fce88bdc343d55093d762daecc6557f1a7d5401/skills/test/test_check_skill_files.py#L2317-L2637)** — `FieldsBoundary`, `BeforeUseOrdering` and `InstalledWorkPlannerModel`; the fixture `prerequisites-756aaf9.json` feeds the 13-artifact cycle test.

## Risks and Watch Points

- **Lexical candidate heuristic.**
  `BEHAVIORS`, `ACTORS` and the agentive and passive patterns ([L1510-L1546](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/6fce88bdc343d55093d762daecc6557f1a7d5401/skills/scripts/check_skill_files.py#L1510-L1546)) decide candidates from fixed word lists. Synonyms outside them are missed and new actor nouns add noise; candidates fail nothing, so drift shows only in printed output.
- **Recursive cycle search.**
  `connect` inside `before_use_cycles` recurses once per node on a path ([L1698-L1717](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/6fce88bdc343d55093d762daecc6557f1a7d5401/skills/scripts/check_skill_files.py#L1698-L1717)); a chain deeper than Python's recursion limit (about 1,000) would raise. Current skill graphs are far smaller.
- **Requirement grammar.**
  `BEFORE_USE` ([L1607-L1608](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/blob/6fce88bdc343d55093d762daecc6557f1a7d5401/skills/scripts/check_skill_files.py#L1607-L1608)) matches only `Read` followed by links and `first.` or `before …`. A read-first requirement phrased otherwise adds no edge, so a cycle through it goes unreported.
- **Reads beyond the roots.**
  The graph follows targets outside the checked roots; a missing or non-Markdown target reads as empty rather than as an unresolved link, which the existing link checks cover separately.

## References

- **R1.** [Pull request #1692](https://github.com/m2ux/workflow-server/pull/1692) — the Changes listing and Test Plan.
